title: [CQ-M07l] JetBrains Accounts tab: VM token action
description:
Slice of CQ-M07 (task-1a8f1d0e199046a289e94a5453d758b8). Design: mem:decision-cq-m07-verified-local-activation, decision 5. Depends on CQ-M07k (task-324d4f53: the `accounts vm-token` CLI and the presence flag) and on CQ-M07o (task-8dbc76d7), so the two JetBrains slices never edit util/TerminalAgentLauncher.kt at the same time.

Objective: the human can mint, replace and remove each rotation account's VM token from the JetBrains Accounts tab, and see which accounts have one, without the plugin ever touching a token.

Deliverable (moe-jetbrains, JetBrains only: VS Code has no Accounts tab; CQ-M07's docs say so):
- An Accounts tab action per account that opens a terminal running `accounts vm-token <id>` (and one for `--remove`), through the same path sign-in uses (TerminalAgentLauncher runAccountsCommand / accountsCommandLine / buildAccountsCommand): the same shells (POWERSHELL, WSL_BASH, BASH), quoting and WSL path handling.
- A per-account VM-token indicator from CQ-M07k's presence flag. A daemon that sends no flag (an older daemon) shows unknown, never present.

NOT in scope: token storage and minting (CQ-M07k); launch routing (CQ-M07o).

Verification: ./gradlew test under the jetbrains-gradle lease (mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease): cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun", or a snapshot run of the exact commit.
definitionOfDone: The action builds `accounts vm-token <id>` and `accounts vm-token <id> --remove` command lines for the POWERSHELL, WSL_BASH and BASH shells with the same quoting as sign-in (JUnit on the pure builder).
The indicator shows present, absent and unknown (flag missing) per account (JUnit on the pure presentation).
The command line carries no token argument and the plugin never reads the token store (JUnit plus code review note in the completion).

implementationPlan.description:
Read the VM-token contract first: the CQ-M07k comment on this task and `mem:task-task-324d4f53cf28486d8bc0de70b6a99b8d-handoff`. The daemon sends `vmToken: boolean` on each ACCOUNTS_UPDATED account, computed from a stat. The plugin never sees a token.

**1. Model.** In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt, `ClaudeAccount` gains a LAST parameter `val vmToken: Boolean? = null`.
- KDoc: whether Moe holds a VM token for this account (for Moe VM jobs, CQ-M07k), as the daemon reports it from a stat. Null when the daemon does not report it (an older daemon); the tab shows that as unknown, never as set. It is never a token.
- The default keeps every existing constructor call compiling.

**2. Parser.** In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt parseClaudeAccount, read `vmToken` as a real JSON boolean only:
`obj.get("vmToken")?.takeIf { it.isJsonPrimitive && it.asJsonPrimitive.isBoolean }?.asBoolean`.
- Everything else gives null: a string ("true", a token-shaped string), a number, JSON null, an object or a missing field.
- Not getStrictBooleanOrDefault: absent must stay distinguishable from false.

**3. Tests in moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJsonTest.kt.**
- In `rotationJson`, give acct-1 `"vmToken": true` and acct-2 `"vmToken": false`, and leave acct-3 without it. In `expectedRotation`, set acct-1 vmToken = true, acct-2 false and acct-3 null.
  - The existing tests `parseAccountRotation reads an ACCOUNTS_UPDATED payload exactly` and `parseState reads the account rotation and each worker's account` then prove true, false and missing.
- In `parseAccountRotation drops bad accounts and reads wrong-typed fields as absent`:
  - acct-3 gets `"vmToken": "sk-ant-oat01-` plus a fake 40-character body plus `"`;
  - acct-4 gets `"vmToken": 1`;
  - both parse to null, so the expected objects keep the default;
  - add `assertFalse(rotation.toString().contains("sk-ant"))`: a token-shaped value never survives parsing.
implementationPlan.note: ClaudeAccount.vmToken: Boolean? = null (trailing, KDoc). parseClaudeAccount reads vmToken only when it is a JSON boolean primitive. MoeJsonTest: rotationJson acct-1 true / acct-2 false / acct-3 missing (expectedRotation true/false/null); the drops test gives acct-3 a token-shaped string and acct-4 the number 1, both null, plus assertFalse(rotation.toString().contains("sk-ant")); new literal-table test (true/false/"true"/"false"/1/0/null/{}/[]). Gradle runs once at step 4 per plan. Pre-existing dirty paths from other sessions (.moe/*, docs/*, packages/moe-daemon/*) untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Add the presentation, the bundle keys and their JUnit. This is pure code: AccountPresentation.kt stays free of IntelliJ classes.

**moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/AccountPresentation.kt**
- **Row.** AccountRow gains a LAST field `vmToken: AccountText`: VM_TOKEN_STATE_PRESENT when the account's flag is true, VM_TOKEN_STATE_ABSENT when it is false and VM_TOKEN_STATE_UNKNOWN when it is null (DoD 2).
- **Actions.** AccountActions gains `setVmToken` and `removeVmToken`. With `account` the selected account:
  - setVmToken = cli && selected && account.vmToken != null;
  - removeVmToken = cli && selected && account.vmToken == true.
  Like sign-in, they need only the CLI's paths, not the connection. Add a comment on why an unknown flag disables both: the flag and the `vm-token` command ship in the same daemon (CQ-M07k), so a daemon that sends no flag runs a CLI that refuses the command.
- **Arguments.** `fun vmTokenArgs(accountId: String, remove: Boolean): List<String>` returns listOf("vm-token", accountId), or listOf("vm-token", accountId, "--remove").
  - KDoc: these are the only VM-token words the plugin passes. A token is never an argument, and the plugin never reads Moe's token store, only the daemon's flag.
  - Do NOT write the store's folder name anywhere under src/main, not even in a comment: the tripwire test below scans for it.
- **AccountKeys.**
  - COLUMN_VM_TOKEN, appended last to COLUMNS.
  - VM_TOKEN_STATE_PRESENT, VM_TOKEN_STATE_ABSENT and VM_TOKEN_STATE_UNKNOWN, under the prefix `moe.accounts.vmTokenState.`.
  - BUTTON_SET_VM_TOKEN and BUTTON_REMOVE_VM_TOKEN.
  - Dialog keys under `moe.accounts.vmToken.`: VM_TOKEN_SET_TITLE, VM_TOKEN_SET_CONFIRM ({0} = label), VM_TOKEN_REMOVE_TITLE, VM_TOKEN_REMOVE_CONFIRM ({0} = label) and VM_TOKEN_UNSUPPORTED.

**moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties**
ASCII only. No apostrophe in a text with a placeholder: MessageFormat drops it, and the bundle guard fails on it.
- moe.accounts.column.vmToken=VM token
- moe.accounts.vmTokenState.present=Set
- moe.accounts.vmTokenState.absent=Not set
- moe.accounts.vmTokenState.unknown=Unknown
- moe.accounts.button.setVmToken=Set VM token...
- moe.accounts.button.removeVmToken=Remove VM token...
- moe.accounts.vmToken.setTitle=Set VM Token
- moe.accounts.vmToken.setConfirm=Create a long-lived Claude token for {0}? Moe keeps it only to run the agents of this account in a Moe VM, and it replaces any token already set. A terminal tab opens: sign in with the same Claude account, then paste the token claude prints at the hidden prompt.
- moe.accounts.vmToken.removeTitle=Remove VM Token
- moe.accounts.vmToken.removeConfirm=Remove the VM token for {0}? Moe then cannot run the agents of this account in a Moe VM until a new token is set. This deletes the copy Moe keeps; it does not revoke the token.
- moe.accounts.vmToken.unsupported=This Moe daemon does not report VM tokens. Restart it after updating Moe.

Also change the existing moe.accounts.remove.confirm, because CQ-M07k rev 2 deletes the token on every removal:
`Remove {0} from the list? Remove only keeps its Claude sign-in on this machine and deletes its VM token. Sign out and remove signs it out first, in a terminal tab.`

**moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/AccountPresentationTest.kt**
- **Existing tests.** Append text(VM_TOKEN_STATE_UNKNOWN) to every expected AccountRow, since the helper accounts carry no flag. Add setVmToken = false and removeVmToken = false to `none`. Every other expectation stays the same.
- **`the VM token column shows set, not set and unknown`.** Accounts with vmToken true, false and null give PRESENT, ABSENT and UNKNOWN, in that order (DoD 2).
- **`VM token actions need the CLI, a selection and a daemon that reports the flag`.**
  - flag true: both;
  - false: set only;
  - null: neither;
  - cli = null: neither;
  - no selection: neither;
  - connected = false: the same as connected.
- **`VM token command lines quote like sign-in in every shell` (DoD 1, 3).**
  - Assert vmTokenArgs' exact lists.
  - Then call TerminalAgentLauncher.buildAccountsCommand with the same fixtures as the three accounts-command tests in moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/util/TerminalAgentLauncherTest.kt: the PowerShell O'Brien and D:\moe$ paths, the WSL /mnt paths, and the bash o'neil path.
  - Cover each shell with both set and remove, asserted as exact strings ending in the quoted words 'vm-token' 'acct-1', or 'vm-token' 'acct-1' '--remove'.
  - Import com.moe.util.TerminalAgentLauncher and its internal AccountsShell, which are visible within the module. Do not edit TerminalAgentLauncherTest.kt.
- **`the plugin never names the VM token store` (DoD 3 tripwire).**
  - Walk File("src/main") over .kt, .java, .properties and .xml files; Gradle runs tests in the module dir.
  - Fail unless AccountPresentation.kt is among the files, so the test never passes vacuously.
  - Then assert no file contains "claude-vm-tokens".
- **Bundle guard.**
  - Raise the key count from 61 to 72 (11 new keys).
  - Add "moe.accounts.vmTokenState." to presentationPrefixes, and emit rows covering true, false and null so all three state keys are formatted.
  - panelArgs gains VM_TOKEN_SET_CONFIRM to 1 and VM_TOKEN_REMOVE_CONFIRM to 1.

implementationPlan.description:
Wire moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/AccountsPanel.kt. This is Swing; JUnit covers the pure parts in step 2.

- **Buttons.** Append two buttons to the button row, after removeButton:
  - setVmTokenButton (BUTTON_SET_VM_TOKEN) calls setVmToken();
  - removeVmTokenButton (BUTTON_REMOVE_VM_TOKEN) calls removeVmToken().
- **setVmToken().**
  - account = selected() ?: return.
  - Messages.showOkCancelDialog(project, message(VM_TOKEN_SET_CONFIRM, account.label), message(VM_TOKEN_SET_TITLE), message(VM_TOKEN_SET_TITLE), message(CANCEL), Messages.getQuestionIcon()).
  - On OK: runCli(AccountPresentation.vmTokenArgs(account.id, remove = false)).
- **removeVmToken().** The same, with VM_TOKEN_REMOVE_CONFIRM, VM_TOKEN_REMOVE_TITLE and Messages.getWarningIcon(). On OK: runCli(AccountPresentation.vmTokenArgs(account.id, remove = true)).
  - Each action captures account.id BEFORE its dialog, so a refresh while the dialog is open cannot retarget it.
- **updateActions().**
  - Enable the buttons from allowed.setVmToken and allowed.removeVmToken.
  - When the CLI is known and the selected account's flag is null, give both buttons the VM_TOKEN_UNSUPPORTED tooltip; otherwise no tooltip.

Error handling:
- runCli already handles a missing terminal: the command goes on the clipboard and a warning dialog opens.
- The CLI prints its own fixed MOE_VM_TOKEN_* failure line in the terminal.
- Cancel, or closing a dialog, runs nothing.
- No new failure path is needed.

comments.author: architect-b520bc90
comments.content:
Contract from CQ-M07k (task-324d4f53, plan rev 1, WORKING). Plan against this; the full contract is in `mem:task-task-324d4f53cf28486d8bc0de70b6a99b8d-handoff`.

**Commands, run in a terminal through the existing accounts path:**
- `accounts vm-token <id>`
  - It runs `claude setup-token` interactively under the account's config folder, then asks the person to paste the token at a HIDDEN prompt on the same terminal. The terminal must therefore be interactive, with stdin attached, exactly as `accounts login <id>` is.
  - Exit 0 on success. Exit 1 with one fixed line on failure: MOE_VM_TOKEN_MINT_FAILED, MOE_VM_TOKEN_NOT_STORED, MOE_VM_TOKEN_INVALID, or the existing unknown-account error.
- `accounts vm-token <id> --remove` deletes the token and exits 0, whether or not one existed.
- `accounts remove <id>` now also deletes that account's token.

**Presence flag:** each entry of the ACCOUNTS_UPDATED `accounts[]` gains `vmToken: boolean`, computed from a stat only (the daemon never opens the token).
- It is typed in accountStore.ts as `AccountViewWithVmToken`, because types/schema.ts is held by WT-19. The plugin's Kotlin model should parse it as optional.
- A missing field (an older daemon) shows unknown, never present, per this task's DoD.

The plugin never reads or passes a token; it only launches those commands.
